read_prompt: Read the image file {path}. It is an enlarged crop of a few printed lines from one column of an 1854 Hebrew-English lexicon (Gesenius, Robinson translation). Transcribe every complete printed text line exactly, one array element per printed line, top to bottom. Preserve spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, printed abbreviations, section marks and end-of-line hyphenation. Hebrew, Aramaic, Arabic, Syriac, Greek and Ethiopic must be Unicode text with every visible vowel point, dagesh, shin or sin dot, accent and diacritic, and with no point that is not printed; write them in logical order with no bidi control characters, keep the words of a right-to-left phrase in the order they are read, and keep the printed left-to-right order of separate items in a list. Transcribe the letters actually printed even when they are not the dictionary spelling: never insert or drop a vav or yod, and never replace a form with a more familiar one. Distinguish Arabic from Syriac by the letter shapes. If a line is only partially visible at the top or bottom edge, omit it entirely rather than guessing. Never add, reorder, translate, normalise or omit anything that is fully visible. If the crop contains no text, return an empty array.

אִטֵּר m. adj. (r. אָטַר) shut up, bound,
i. e. impeded. Judg. 3, 15. 20, 16 אִטֵּר
יַד יְמִינוֹ impeded as to his right hand,
i. e. who cannot use the right hand free-
ly, and hence i. q. left-handed. Arab.
أَطَرَ Conj. V, to be impeded; comp.
عقل to bind, to tie, transferred also to
the tongue, like Engl. tongue-tied.
* אַי, constr. אֵי 1. Interrog. adverb,
where? c. suff. אַיֶּכָּה where art thou?
Gen. 3, 9. אַיּוֹ where is he? Ex. 2, 20.
אַיָּם where are they? Is. 19, 12. More
freq. with He parag. אַיֵּה q. v.—This
particle seems to have arisen by drop-
ping the Nun from אַיִן II, (q. v. in מֵאַיִן
whence?) and this again seems to have
been originally the same as the nega-
tive אַיִן I; just as many other negative
words have also passed over to an in-
terrogative power; comp. Lat. ne, Germ.
nicht wahr? Engl. not so? Hence אַיִן
pr. he is not there, not present, i. q. אֵינֶנּוּ,
comp. Job 14, 10; and interrog. is he not
there? q. d. where is he? In this way
אַיֵּה no. I and II become closely related.

lines.note: The vowel under the aleph of אַתָּה is a short horizontal patach (same form as in line 1's אַתָּה), not a qamets with a descending stem; Reading B's אָתָּה is wrong.

lines.text: strictly Lat. ‘undenam populi? undenam
urbis?’ as Plaut. unde gentium? Odyss.
1. 170 πόθεν ἀνδρῶν. c) אֵי לָזֹאת where-
fore? why? from לָזֹאת therefore, Jer. 5, 7.
Note. With certain other particles
אֵי is joined more closely, so as to coa-
lesce with them into one word, as אֵיךְ,
אֵיכָה, אֵיכֹה, אֵיפֹה, q. v. The same use
of this particle is found in Syr. ܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ
in what way? how? ܐܰܝܡܶܟܳܐ whence?
lines.draft: in what way ? how ? ܐܰܝܡܶܟܳܐ whence ?
lines.reread: in what way ? how ? ܐܲܝܡܸܟܵܐ whence ?
lines.note: The Syriac word is printed in Serto with Western Greek-style vowel glyphs (ptāḥā ܰ on olaph, rbāṣā ܶ on mim, the small "o"-shaped zqāphā ܳ on kaph/final olaph), not the Eastern dot-vowels of Reading B. Letters ܐܝܡܟܐ agree in both readings.

lines.text: ܐܰܝܢܳܐ who? Chald. אֵידַיִן who then? אֵידָם
lines.draft: ܐܰܝܢܳܐ who ? Chald. אֵידֵין who then ? אֵידָם
lines.reread: ܐܲܝܢܵܐ who ? Chald. אֵידַיִן who then ? אֵידָם
lines.note: The Syriac is printed in Serto with Western vowel signs (wedge-shaped pthaha over the first alef, ring-shaped zqapha over nun), matching Reading A, not B's Eastern points. But the Chaldee word is clearly printed plene with five letters, אֵידַיִן (a yod with hiriq visible between dalet and nun), matching Reading B, not A's אֵידֵין.

lines.text: id. Eth. አይቴ where? how?—In Prov.
31, 4 Keri וּלְרוֹזְנִים אֵי שֵׁכָר, render: nor
for princes [to say], Where is strong
drink? See in אַי no. 1.
I. אִי contr. for אֱוִי, (as כִּי for כְּוִי, דִּי
lines.draft: I. אִי contr. for אֱוִי, (as כִּי for כְּוִי, רִי
lines.reread: I. אִי contr. for אֱוִי, (as כִּי for כְּוִי, דַּי
lines.note: Final word: the letter is dalet (top bar projects right past the stem, matching the דְּוִי on the next line), so A's resh is wrong; but the vowel beneath is a single dot (hiriq), not a patah, so B's דַּי is also wrong. Printed is דִּי (dagesh dot visible in the dalet), parallel to the following "for דְּוִי".

lines.text: for דְּוַי, comp. Lehrg. p. 510,) m. perhaps
lines.draft: for רְוִי, comp. Lehrg. p. 510,) m. perhaps
lines.reread: for דְּוַי, comp. Lehrg. p. 510,) m. perhaps
lines.note: The first Hebrew letter carries a dagesh (dot inside) and sheva, so it is דּ not ר, and the vav has a patach (horizontal stroke) beneath it, not a hiriq — matching Reading B and completing "דַּי for דְּוַי" begun at the end of line 3.
